middle.heading: About Me
middle.intro: I’m a software engineer with 5+ years of experience building reactive, user-friendly web components. I’m also an amateur frog enthusiast with 28+ years experience. My recent work has largely been in TypeScript, SolidJS, and Angular, but I’m more interested in providing a rich user experience than in using any particular framework or language. Lately I’ve been dabbling in React, and I’m enjoying it so far. When it comes to amphibians, most of my hands-on experience has been in northwestern Pennsylvania, but I’m interested in critters of all kinds and locales.
middle.contact: Here’s {resume}, or you can {email} directly. I’m also on {linkedIn}, and you can check out the code for this site on my {gitHub}.

entry01.title: Eastern Cricket Frog
entry01.blurb: Acris crepitans. A small frog with rough skin. Its color can be greenish, brown, tan, or yellow.

entry02.title: Eastern American Toad
entry02.blurb: Anaxyrus americanus. A medium-sized lumpy frog. Its color can be brown, red, olive, or gray.

entry03.title: Fowler’s Toad
entry03.blurb: Anaxyrus fowleri. Get a load of this lunatic. A medium-sized frog. Its color is typically brown to gray.

entry04.title: Cope’s Gray Treefrog
entry04.blurb: Hyla chrysoscelis. Just try and look away from this moderate-sized beauty. Its color is typically gray or greenish gray.

entry05.title: Gray Treefrog
entry05.blurb: Hyla versicolor. Honestly not sure why Cope prefers the other one because this is another moderate-sized frog. Its color is also usually gray or greenish gray.

entry06.title: American Bullfrog
entry06.blurb: Lithobates catesbeianus. A LARGE frog. Its color typically falls between green and brown.

entry07.title: Green Frog
entry07.blurb: Lithobates clamitans. You are never going to guess what color this frog is. Of note it is a large frog.

entry08.title: Atlantic Coast Leopard Frog
entry08.blurb: Lithobates kauffeldi. Spots on this guy like you wouldn’t believe. This is a medium-sized frog. Its color can vary from bright green to dark brown.

entry09.title: Pickerel Frog
entry09.blurb: Lithobates palustris. Walleye’ll be. A moderate-sized frog. This frog’s color is usually brown or tan.

entry10.title: Northern Leopard Frog
entry10.blurb: Lithobates pipiens. This is a moderate-sized frog whose color is often bright green, dark greenish brown, or brown.

entry11.title: Wood Frog
entry11.blurb: Lithobates sylvaticus. As close to a tree as a frog can be. This is a moderate-sized frog with a color that can be gray brown, dark brown, or reddish brown.

entry12.title: Mountain Chorus Frog
entry12.blurb: Pseudacris brachyphona. If you’re feeling froggy jump. This bad boy is a small frog whose color can be anywhere between tan and light brown.

entry13.title: Spring Peeper
entry13.blurb: Pseudacris crucifer. Peep this fella. A small frog with a color that is mostly different shades of brown.

entry14.title: Upland Chorus Frog
entry14.blurb: Pseudacris feriarum. This is a small frog. Its main color can be gray, tan, or greenish brown.

entry15.title: New Jersey Chorus Frog
entry15.blurb: Pseudacris kalmi. The king of chorus frogs and a small frog. Its color can be gray, tan, or greenish brown.

entry16.title: Western Chorus Frog
entry16.blurb: Pseudacris triseriata. It’s no New Jersey Chorus Frog, but it might be the stripiest of the lot. A small frog whose main color can be gray, tan, or greenish brown.

entry17.title: Eastern Spadefoot
entry17.blurb: Scaphiopus holbrookii. A small frog with the coolest name in town. Its color can be dark brown, gray, or blackish gray.

entry18.title: Greg
entry18.blurb: Felis catus. A beautiful medium-sized tabby cat. He’s often found chewing through treat bags, lounging in sunbeams, or being loud when you’re trying to sleep.

entry19.title: Sophie
entry19.blurb: Felis catus. A beautiful small-sized tuxedo cat. She’s often found sleeping on warm clean laundry, hiding beneath a couch, or perched in a lap.

about.heading: About
about.intro: This site is an exploration into developing with Claude. I mainly used the Opus 5.5 model, though I used Fable 5.1 for some of the bigger tasks. My last Claude assisted project was built with Sonnet 5.5, and details about its construction can be found on my GitHub. This time around I wanted to try to lean more into AI assisted development and put something together rapidly. I did less line by line code checking, instead leaning on fresh Claude sessions for code reviews. I also used the previous project as a style guide, and that helped to speed up development. I still had Claude throw together plan documents for bigger changes. I find it reduces the number of miscommunications and helps catch some unexpected behaviors before implementation.
about.body: All images and drawings on the site are my own, so no need for licensing. I’m just a casual frog enjoyer, and I didn’t want to wing it, so all frog facts on this site (excluding those about cats) came from paherps.com.
